newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up on technicals, players sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up on technicals, players sidelined.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange saw a small technical rebound Thursday, closing up slightly in lethargic trade as investors continued to languish on the sidelines, brokers said.
But the market will likely succumb to its underlying weakness Friday, with volume expected even below the meager 18 million sol ($7 million) average for the month, they added.
The General Index climbed 0.16 percent to 1,424.8 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 0.48 percent to 2,005.6 points.

Due to the economy's slower-than-expected growth, equities prices have fallen steadily over the last few months and investors do not expect any good news in the short-term to lift the market, brokers said.

"For now, the market is going to depend on the government's ability to improve the current economic situation. Bearing this in mind, it seems we will continue to see inertia on the exchange," said Jos Carranza of local brokerage Plusvalor.
The government estimates the economy will grow around 2.5 percent this year, down from 7.0 percent last year.
The government predicts the economy will not start to pick up noticeably until the first quarter next year.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per edged up 0.80 percent to 5.04 soles in low volume of 225,000 shares, according to preliminary figures.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start last week, closed down 0.87 percent at 3.40 soles in trade of 522,000 shares.
In a total of 1,230 trades, volume was estimated at 12.1 million soles ($4.7 million), with 25 stocks up, 19 down and 16 stable.
